negative_findings.description: Searches for a standalone 'Kosovo segment' in RBI group reporting returned only the aggregated 'Southeastern Europe' segment (Albania, BiH, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kosovo, Romania, Serbia). Kosovo-level figures appear, if at all, in country tables/appendices rather than as an IFRS 8 reportable segment.
negative_findings.result_summary: SEE segment ~19% of group income in the Q1/2026 presentation per search snippet; no evidence found of a Kosovo-only reportable segment.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must target country tables and appendix pages inside PDFs, not segment note headings; expect derivation rather than direct extraction.

negative_findings.description: Turkish-language searches for TEB A.Ş. investor material naming 'TEB Sh.A. Kosova' as an iştirak/bağlı ortaklık returned only general TEB annual reports and the BNP Paribas/Çolakoğlu ownership structure; no Kosovo-specific parent disclosure surfaced in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Kosovo detail for TEB appears to live mainly at the local entity (teb-kos.com annual reports), not in the Turkish parent's IR pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For the TEB chain the local subsidiary report is likely the primary source; KAP notification search should still be probed directly before concluding the parent publishes nothing.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language querying produced useful results only for the NLB/Ljubljana disclosure chain; no Serbian-language parent-group disclosure route was found for the Kosovo units of Raiffeisen, ProCredit, TEB, BKT or Ziraat.
negative_findings.result_summary: Serbian terms used: 'rezultati', 'izveštaj', 'objave', 'Ljubljanska berza', 'banka'. Only NLB/LJSE material returned.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian is probably not a productive collection language for parent-group disclosures in this cell; effort should be reallocated to sq, en, de, tr and sl.

negative_findings.description: No Albanian-language reporting/disclosure vocabulary was found attached to Ziraat's Kosovo presence — it appears to operate as branches under a country directorate rather than a separately reporting legal entity.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ziraat annual reports list a Kosovo Country Directorate and branches in Prishtina, Prizren, Peja, Ferizaj; no Albanian-language 'pasqyrat financiare' page located for the Kosovo operation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ziraat Kosovo data may only be obtainable from the Turkish parent report or the Kosovo regulator, not from a local-language corporate disclosure.

negative_findings.description: https://www.ziraat-kosova.com/ was referenced inside Ziraat annual-report content but was not independently fetched in this pass; its liveness and whether it hosts reports are unconfirmed.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Must be checked by the deterministic verification pass before being treated as a collection target.

brief: Kosovo's banking sector is overwhelmingly foreign-owned, so the richest and most comparable disclosure sits one level up, in parent-group IR material published in Vienna (RBI), Ljubljana (NLB), Frankfurt (ProCredit Holding), Istanbul (TEB A.Ş., Ziraat, Çalık) and Tirana (BKT). Three of these chains — RBI, NLB and ProCredit — are listed or regulated issuers with dense, predictable, machine-collectable artefacts (annual and quarterly report PDFs on stable paths, quarterly investor decks, statutory ad-hoc feeds via EQS and LJSE SEOnet), and NLB is the most granular on Kosovo specifically. The Turkish-controlled chains (TEB, Ziraat, BKT/Çalık) disclose far less at country level: KAP notifications and Turkish integrated annual reports carry only partial Kosovo detail, and for BKT and Ziraat the local entity or the Kosovo regulator may be the only quantitative route. The clearest untapped opportunity is regulatory country-by-country reporting and Pillar 3 annexes of the EU parents, which name Kosovo explicitly with turnover, profit, tax and headcount and would give a consistent cross-group time series.
